area: Adversarial verification: Photon and CREAO agent tooling (MCP servers, docs MCP, llms.txt, skills, CLI, SDKs, APIs)

items.name: Photon Docs MCP (Mintlify docs search, https://photon.codes/docs/mcp)
items.install: Remote streamable-HTTP endpoint, no auth. Command (inferred from the standard Claude Code syntax, not published by Photon): `claude mcp add --transport http photon-docs https://photon.codes/docs/mcp`. CONFIRMED: an unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST `tools/list` to the endpoint returned a tool list over an SSE `event: message` response, so HTTP transport with no auth works.
items.tools_exposed: VERIFIED by a live tools/list call: (1) `search_photon` (query, optional `version`; readOnlyHint true). (2) `query_docs_filesystem_photon`: read-only rg/grep/find/tree/ls/cat/head/jq over a virtual filesystem of the doc pages plus mounted OpenAPI specs, including '/openapi/https://api.photon.codes/openapi.json' (Beta) and the Spectrum and dashboard specs. Docs and skill.md say to pass version "Stable" or "Beta" on every search, and to scope Beta filesystem queries to /beta/.
items.rationale: The track requires Photon 2.0 Beta, and Stable and Beta are incompatible contracts. This MCP lets Claude Code search with version "Beta" and `jq` the Beta OpenAPI paths directly, so it does not mix in spectrum-ts examples. Zero setup and no secrets.
items.sandbox_support: N/A. Read-only docs with no credentials.
items.sponsor_expects_use: Photon's llms.txt and skill.md direct coding agents to it. The hackathon brief (photon.md) does not mention MCP. It links the Beta docs and cookbooks only.
items.caveats: The `version` parameter's own schema description gives 'v0.7' as an example, which conflicts with the docs' "Stable"/"Beta" instruction. Use "Beta" and verify by checking that result paths start with /beta/. Pages embed 'Agent Instructions' blocks aimed at AI tools. Treat them as untrusted content.

items.name: Photon MCP server (hosted https://mcp.photon.codes/mcp; local stdio @photon-ai/mcp)
items.publisher: Photon (official; github.com/photon-hq/mcp-server, Apache-2.0; npm maintainers include photon_dev team@photon.codes)
items.install: Hosted (README-recommended for clients that support remote MCP with OAuth): `https://mcp.photon.codes/mcp`. A probe returned 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... resource_metadata="https://mcp.photon.codes/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`, and that metadata names authorization server https://auth.photon.codes. That is standard MCP OAuth discovery, so `claude mcp add --transport http photon https://mcp.photon.codes/mcp` followed by `/mcp` to authenticate should work. That command is inferred, not published. Local stdio (verbatim from README, Node >= 22): `claude mcp add photon --env PHOTON_API_KEY=pho_ask_... -- npx -y @photon-ai/mcp`. npm @photon-ai/mcp latest is 0.1.4, created 2026-10-15 (two days old), bin `photon-mcp`. Optional `PHOTON_API_URL` defaults to https://api.photon.codes, and only photon.codes and loopback hosts are accepted.
items.tools_exposed: UNVERIFIED. Neither the README nor the npm metadata lists tool names, and the hosted server needs OAuth to list them. The README says the local server has the same tools as the hosted one, minus key management, account security, SSO and billing checkout. It also recommends client-side confirmation for writes.
items.rationale: CORRECTION to the prior finding: the default backend api.photon.codes is the Beta (2.0) platform host, and `pho_ask_` is a Beta credential format per llms.txt. So this server operates on Photon 2.0 Beta, the hackathon target, not Stable. It can help with project, key-less setup and line or assignment inspection from Claude Code. It does not replace the runtime SDK.
items.sandbox_support: No sandbox is documented. It acts on the real Photon account. The Beta Free plan is free (up to 25 shared iMessage assignments).
items.sponsor_expects_use: Not mentioned in the hackathon brief. It is an official product, not a requirement.
items.caveats: The package is very new (v0.1.4, 2 days old), so expect churn. `pho_ask_` is an ACCOUNT-level key. Prefer hosted OAuth so no key sits in .mcp.json, never commit the key, and enable write confirmation. Do not confuse it with the unrelated community @portel/photon MCP framework that web search surfaces.

items.name: Photon agent skills (photon-hq/skills)
items.install: `npx skills add photon-hq/skills --skill <name>` (verbatim). Skills: imessage, chat-adapter-imessage, buildspace-ci-cd, spectrum, photon-cli.
items.tools_exposed: Not an MCP. These are SKILL.md instruction packages. The imessage skill covers the 'v3 local SDK object API' and hosted HTTP/gRPC entry points, and treats @photon-ai/advanced-imessage-kit as legacy. spectrum covers spectrum-ts. photon-cli covers @photon-ai/cli.
items.rationale: DOWNGRADED from high. No skill targets the Beta 2.0 API (@photon-ai/api, api.photon.codes/v1). All of them cover Stable or Spectrum surfaces. That is useful background on iMessage semantics, but it risks steering the coding agent toward the wrong contract for a Beta-qualified project. The docs MCP, llms.txt and the Beta OpenAPI spec are the better Beta aids.
items.sandbox_support: N/A
items.sponsor_expects_use: Not in the hackathon brief. The CLI README points agents at the photon-cli skill.
items.caveats: If you install these skills, tell the agent explicitly that the project uses Beta and that skill examples are Stable. Review each SKILL.md before installing (third-party instructions).

items.name: Photon llms.txt, skill.md, .md page exports, and OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs
items.install: No install. Fetch the URLs: https://photon.codes/docs/llms.txt (sections '## Stable: ...' and '## Beta: Overview/Messaging/Cookbooks/API Client/API Reference'), https://photon.codes/docs/skill.md (version-selection procedure), https://photon.codes/docs/llms-full.txt (Stable full text), any page with a `.md` suffix, and specs https://api.photon.codes/openapi.json and https://api.photon.codes/asyncapi.yaml (Beta), https://spectrum.photon.codes/openapi/json (Stable), and https://photon.codes/docs/api-reference/dashboard-openapi.json.
items.tools_exposed: N/A (static docs)
items.rationale: Zero setup. llms.txt gives a Beta vs Stable signal table: Beta uses packages `@photon-ai/api`/`photonhq-api`, host https://api.photon.codes/v1, project IDs prefixed `pho_prj_`, and Bearer `pho_ask_`/`pho_sk_`/JWT credentials. Stable uses spectrum.photon.codes with HTTP Basic auth. Beta event delivery is Socket.IO with cursor replay (/docs/beta/websocket/*). Put the table into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.
items.sandbox_support: N/A
items.sponsor_expects_use: The hackathon brief links the Beta docs and cookbooks.
items.caveats: The brief says the Beta docs are 'still being written'. skill.md warns that Beta CLI releases may not provision production credentials.

items.name: Photon Beta API client libraries (photon-hq/api)
items.install: Verbatim from the repo README: `npm install @photon-ai/api` (npm 0.5.0, modified 2026-10-16, repo photon-hq/api), `pip install photonhq-api` (PyPI 0.5.0, author Photon; the import name is `photon_api`), `cargo add photonhq-api`, `go get github.com/photon-hq/api/packages/go`. CORRECTIONS: the Python package is `photonhq-api`, not `photon_api` (`photon_api` and `photon-api` return 404 on PyPI), and the Rust crate is `photonhq-api`, not `photon-ai-api`.
items.tools_exposed: N/A (SDK). Shared-line assignment (e.g. CreateSharedLineAssignment), messaging, and Socket.IO event delivery.
items.rationale: This is the runtime integration that qualifies for the track ('built on Photon 2.0 and live on at least one Photon channel').
items.sandbox_support: The Beta quickstart uses a shared line with your own phone number as sender. The Free plan includes 25 shared iMessage assignments. No separate sandbox environment is documented.
items.sponsor_expects_use: Yes, Photon 2.0 Beta is mandatory for the track.
items.caveats: CRITICAL for a GROUP-planning agent, verified on primary sources. The Beta iMessage page says 'A shared assignment supports direct conversations, not group chats' and 'a shared line cannot send an unsolicited first message'. The plans page lists dedicated iMessage lines as Business-only at $250/line/month (Free and Pro: 'Not available'). photon.md also says group chat on iMessage needs a dedicated line. Ask Photon staff for a dedicated line before designing around iMessage group threads, or plan a fallback such as 1:1 fan-out per member. Keep pho_sk_/pho_ask_ keys in server env only.

items.name: Photon Stable SDKs (spectrum-ts, @photon-ai/advanced-imessage) and deploy templates
items.install: npm `spectrum-ts` (12.11.0, maintainer photon_dev, repo photon-hq/spectrum-ts) and `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` (2.3.0, repo photon-hq/advanced-imessage-ts). The photon-hq org also has `railway-imessage-template` ('private iMessage agent on Railway with Photon Spectrum and Codex') and `render-imessage-template`.
items.tools_exposed: N/A (SDKs). Stable docs cover group rename, membership, polls, reactions, and a credential-free terminal provider.
items.rationale: These are Stable or Spectrum, not Photon 2.0 Beta. Using them likely does not satisfy the track rule. They are useful only as reference for iMessage UX patterns, or for local terminal-provider testing of conversation logic.
items.sandbox_support: spectrum-ts terminal provider (no credentials)
items.caveats: Do not mix Stable code into the Beta project (skill.md: 'Don't mix package names, commands, auth, or routes across versions').

items.name: Photon CLI (@photon-ai/cli, binaries `photon`/`pho`) and Beta `photon-cli`
items.install: `npx @photon-ai/cli login` or `npm install -g @photon-ai/cli` (Node >= 18; npm 2.2.0, last modified 2026-08-04). Auth is `photon login` device flow or `PHOTON_TOKEN`. Env vars: PHOTON_API_HOST, PHOTON_PROJECT_ID, PHOTON_CONFIG_DIR. Command groups: projects (ls/show/create/update/delete/regenerate-secret/open/upgrade/check-phone), spectrum (users/lines/platforms/profile/avatar), billing (plans/show/checkout/manage), profile, login/whoami/auth status, config, ping, update.
items.tools_exposed: N/A (CLI)
items.rationale: DOWNGRADED. Per skill.md and llms.txt, @photon-ai/cli is the STABLE (Spectrum) CLI, and the repo README targets app.photon.codes and Spectrum commands. The Beta CLI is named `photon-cli` (`photon project list`), but no install path is documented. IMPORTANT NEW FINDING: the npm package literally named `photon-cli` is NOT Photon's. It was created 2022-02-01, last version 1.2.4 (2022), maintainer 'photon-kits' (evan@something.surf), with no photon-hq repository link. Do NOT `npm install photon-cli`. For Beta, use the dashboard, the hosted Photon MCP, or the API.
items.sandbox_support: None documented
items.sponsor_expects_use: Not mentioned in the hackathon brief.
items.caveats: Never let an agent run `billing checkout`, `projects delete` or `regenerate-secret` unattended. Possible typosquat or name-collision risk with npm `photon-cli`.

items.name: CREAO CLI API (/v1) and API Trigger (capi_), plus Developer Platform /v2
items.install: No MCP and no shell CLI. '/v1' REST at developer.creao.ai/v1/* with `cr_sk_` Account API keys from Developer Console. Endpoints verified in llms.txt: POST/GET/PATCH /v1/agents, POST /v1/agents/{id}/edits, POST/GET /v1/runs, POST /v1/realtime/runs (NDJSON), /v1/super-agent/runs, /v1/agents/{id}/memory and /files, /v1/workspaces, /v1/secrets, /v1/skills, rooms (SSE), webhooks, /v1/account/usage. App-scoped `capi_` API Trigger keys come from agent.creao.ai (/pro/api-trigger). /v2 Hosted Developer Platform docs are at https://developer.creao.ai/docs, and its llms.txt is at https://developer.creao.ai/docs/llms.txt (fetched, HTTP 200), which states it documents '/v2 only', separate from /v1 and from agent.creao.ai.
items.tools_exposed: REST endpoints listed above
items.rationale: The bot backend calls the saved CREAO agent through API Trigger or /v1/runs and receives results by webhook. The CREAO brief says runs take minutes, there is no live token streaming on the API Trigger, so design async, and keys stay server-side.
items.sandbox_support: No sandbox. Runs spend real credits, and the hackathon grants an upgraded account with top-ups via Discord or the booth.
items.sponsor_expects_use: Yes. The brief's 'Build with: API Trigger + webhooks, connectors, Browser Use, your own tools' and its multi-agent tip ('Coordinate specialized role agents through the API Trigger, with keys stored in Secrets and conversation continuity via threadId').
items.caveats: agent.docs.creao.ai did not resolve from this machine (curl status 000). docs.creao.ai served the content. NEW: llms.txt says 'Scheduled runs ... require Pro Plus or higher'. Confirm that the hackathon-upgraded account tier includes scheduled runs. Never put cr_sk_ or capi_ keys in coding-agent prompts or client code.

items.name: CREAO connectors (MCP-based) including CUSTOM MCP servers, plus CREAO Connect device pairing
items.install: Built-in connectors are added in-app (Skills page > Connectors). The list includes Notion, Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Drive, Outlook, Teams, Asana, Linear, Discord, Telegram, GitHub and more. CORRECTION to the prior finding: CREAO's trust and safety docs (llms-full.txt) list a connector category 'Custom MCP servers | API key, bearer token, or none | Tool schemas fetched from user-specified HTTPS endpoints during setup or refresh'. Separately, 'CREAO Connect' pairs your own computer or server (via CLI or GUI) so the agent can run local capabilities, 'calling a custom MCP server you configure on the device', under a per-device allow/deny/ask consent policy. The step-by-step UI for adding a custom HTTPS MCP connector is NOT described in the user-facing connectors section, which only says to request missing integrations in Discord #feature-requests.
items.tools_exposed: Per-connector MCP tools. A custom MCP server would expose whatever tools the team defines.
items.rationale: The team could expose its own backend (e.g. a thin MCP wrapper over its Visa/Cybersource sandbox calls and Photon send endpoints) as a custom HTTPS MCP server attached to the CREAO agent. That directly targets the CREAO rubric item 'Depth on CREAO (25%) ... Did you extend it with your own tools, APIs, or agents'. The Notion connector and Browser Use cover the rest of the stack.
items.sandbox_support: Connectors act on real connected accounts, so use a test Notion workspace. Writes follow the agent's write-approval setting (per creao.md).
items.sponsor_expects_use: Yes for connectors, Browser Use and 'your own tools' (creao.md). Custom MCP is not named explicitly in the brief.
items.caveats: The existence of custom MCP support is documented only in privacy and security tables, not in a how-to. Confirm the UI path at the CREAO booth or Discord before depending on it. The tool responses and errors of a custom MCP server are forwarded to the selected LLM provider. Expose only sandbox payment operations, require auth on the endpoint, and never expose live payment credentials. CREAO Connect's shell capability on a paired laptop is high-risk, so keep it on 'ask' or 'deny'.

An official published `claude mcp add --transport http` line for either Photon endpoint (both inferred; the docs MCP was confirmed working unauthenticated via tools/list)
Install path for Photon's Beta `photon-cli` (the npm package named `photon-cli` belongs to an unrelated 2022 publisher)
Any Photon skill targeting the Beta 2.0 API
A dedicated iMessage line on Free or Pro: the plans page says Business-only at $250/line/month
A user-facing how-to for adding a custom MCP server connector in CREAO (only privacy and security docs mention it)
CREAO MCP server, CLI binary, SDK or Claude Code plugin for coding agents
Sponsor recommendations of specific AI coding tools in photon.md, creao.md or lahacks.md (none)
npmjs.com web pages returned 403. The registry JSON (registry.npmjs.org) was used instead
notes: I re-fetched every primary source: the GitHub repos, the npm registry JSON, PyPI JSON, photon.codes llms.txt and skill.md, the Beta iMessage and plans pages, docs.creao.ai llms.txt and llms-full.txt, developer.creao.ai/docs, and the local briefs. I also sent read-only JSON-RPC probes to both Photon MCP endpoints. Nothing was installed or modified. Key corrections. (1) The Photon docs MCP is now verified with real tool names (search_photon, query_docs_filesystem_photon) and no auth. (2) The Photon MCP server targets the BETA platform (api.photon.codes, pho_ask_), not Stable, and its hosted endpoint uses standard MCP OAuth (auth.photon.codes). (3) The Python and Rust Beta SDKs are both `photonhq-api` (import `photon_api` in Python). (4) npm `photon-cli` is NOT Photon's (2022, 'photon-kits'), so do not install it. (5) The photon-hq/skills skills are all Stable or Spectrum, so I downgraded them to medium. @photon-ai/cli is the Stable CLI, downgraded to low. (6) CREAO DOES document custom MCP server connectors (HTTPS endpoint, API key, bearer, or no auth) and CREAO Connect device pairing with custom MCP. That reverses the prior 'do not plan on BYO MCP' advice, but the how-to UI is undocumented, so confirm with CREAO staff. A custom MCP wrapping the team's sandbox payment and Photon endpoints would target CREAO's 25% 'Depth on CREAO' criterion. (7) CREAO scheduled runs require Pro Plus or higher, so confirm the hackathon account tier. (8) Biggest build risk, re-confirmed from primary sources: Beta shared iMessage assignments support direct conversations only, with no group chats and no unsolicited first message. Dedicated lines are Business-plan only ($250/line/month). Get a dedicated line from Photon staff or design a 1:1 fan-out fallback. Recommended coding-agent setup: add the Photon docs MCP (http, no auth), optionally the hosted Photon MCP via OAuth with write confirmation, and give agents the llms.txt Beta/Stable signal table and CREAO /v1 docs URLs in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. Keep all keys (pho_*, cr_sk_, capi_, Cybersource) out of prompts and .mcp.json.

area: Visa and Cybersource agent tooling: adversarial re-verification (MCP servers, skills, llms.txt, SDK samples, TAP)

items.name: Cybersource Developer MCP (cybersource-developer-mcp)
items.publisher: Official, from the CyberSource GitHub org. PyPI maintainer is developer@cybersource.com. MIT. Labeled PILOT on the docs page.
items.install: Python >=3.10 (confirmed on PyPI; latest version 0.0.3, uploaded 2026-08-04). The docs page gives these Claude Code CLI steps verbatim: `pip install pipx && pipx ensurepath && pipx install cybersource-developer-mcp`, then `claude mcp add cybersource-developer-mcp cybersource-developer-mcp start`, then `claude mcp list`. The README gives a uvx route (`uvx cybersource-developer-mcp start`). The Claude Code form `claude mcp add cybersource-developer-mcp -- uvx cybersource-developer-mcp start` is adapted from it, not documented. JSON from the docs page (Claude Desktop): {"mcpServers":{"cybersource-developer-mcp":{"type":"stdio","command":"cybersource-developer-mcp","args":["start"],"env":{}}}}. The Cline JSON adds "timeout":300 because the first request for each SDK language downloads that SDK. Optional flags: --data-dir (default ~/.cybersource_developer_mcp/) and --enable-logging. Optional env vars: GITHUB_TOKEN and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. On Windows, enable long path support (260-character limit). Runs locally over stdio. No Cybersource merchant credentials are needed to run it.
items.tools_exposed: Tool names are not documented in the README or on the docs page. Documented capabilities: SDK API documentation, model details, API discovery/listing, setup guides, MLE support and per-API MLE requirements, code templates, guided prompts. SDK languages: the README lists Java, Python, Node.js, PHP, Ruby, .NET and .NET Standard (deprecated). The docs page lists only Java, Python, PHP, Node.js and Ruby, so the two sources disagree on .NET. There is no TypeScript SDK; TypeScript appears only in a sample prompt.
items.rationale: Confirmed as a docs and codegen helper over the official Cybersource REST SDKs, including Node.js. Fits the auth hold / capture / reversal / TMS / Unified Checkout code the team must write. It does not move money. Correction to the earlier finding: the README has no skills section, and only the repo folder skills/ holds the SKILL.md (listed separately). The 'PHP about 3 min' detail was not found in this re-check. The docs only say the first request per language 'can take a few minutes'.
items.sandbox_support: Not applicable: the MCP does not call Cybersource APIs. The docs page links to sandbox registration. The skill documents sandbox host apitest.cybersource.com and production host api.cybersource.com.
items.sponsor_expects_use: Unverified. No source links Visa or Cybersource to an LA Hacks track. LA Hacks 2026 (April 24-26, UCLA) named Amazon, Fetch and Roblox as sponsors in a USC announcement, and Visa/Cybersource do not appear on lahacks.com/sponsor-us. The team should check the event's own sponsor or prize page.
items.caveats: The README disclaims liability and warranty for generated code, and says to review and test it in non-production. Its privacy line reads 'Your code and conversations stay between you and your AI assistant.' Pre-1.0 pilot (0.0.3), so behavior may change. Never put merchant keys or P12 files in the MCP env, in prompts, or in git. The MCP does not need them.

items.name: Cybersource best-practices skill (skills/SKILL.md, name: cybersource-best-practices)
items.publisher: Official, in the same CyberSource repo. MIT.
items.install: The repo documents no install steps. A plausible manual route (inference, not documented): copy the file to <project>/.claude/skills/cybersource-best-practices/SKILL.md for Claude Code, or reference it from AGENTS.md for Codex. It has frontmatter with name, title, description and keywords.
items.tools_exposed: None; it is instructions only. Confirmed content: JWT Shared Secret is recommended (JWT P12 also OK); HTTP Signature is deprecated; OAuth is for ISV/partner use only; MLE works with JWT only. UC v1 flow: POST /uc/v1/sessions returns a captureContext JWT, the client returns a transient token, then POST /pts/v2/payments. Sessions last 15 minutes. allowedPaymentTypes includes PANENTRY/SRC/GOOGLEPAY/APPLEPAY. targetOrigins must match exactly. Verbatim: 'Do NOT use the legacy Microform/Flex endpoint /pts/v2/microform/capture-contexts — that is a deprecated v0.x API'. TMS: store a card with a zero-dollar auth plus TOKEN_CREATE, and pay with the fresh transient token, not the TMS id. Void comes before settlement and refund after. Never auto-retry PROCESSOR_DECLINED code 05. Webhooks must return 200 within 10 seconds, dedupe on webhookId, and use TLS 1.2+. Hosts: apitest / api / api-matest / api-ma.cybersource.com.
items.rationale: Directly encodes the team's hold, capture, void and refund, TMS and UC flows, plus traps that would cost hours at a hackathon. Note: the endpoint it calls deprecated is the legacy capture-contexts endpoint. The llms.txt still lists 'Microform V2' docs, so 'Microform is deprecated' is too broad. The skill steers toward UC v1.
items.sandbox_support: Yes. It documents separate sandbox and production hosts and warns never to mix environments or test cards.
items.caveats: It is guidance; verify against the live docs. It steers agent behavior, so read it before installing.

items.name: Visa Acceptance Agent Toolkit and MCP (@visaacceptance/agent-toolkit, @visaacceptance/mcp)
items.publisher: Official Visa Acceptance GitHub org (visaacceptance/agent-toolkit, MIT). The npm package repository field points to that repo. Pilot.
items.install: Node 18+. `npm install @visaacceptance/agent-toolkit` (Vercel AI SDK). MCP per the README: `npx -y @visaacceptance/mcp --tools=all --merchant-id=... --api-key-id=... --secret-key=...`. The npm registry shows @visaacceptance/mcp 0.0.96 with bin 'mcp' and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.11.0. Claude Code form (adapted, not documented): `claude mcp add visa-acceptance -- npx -y @visaacceptance/mcp --tools=all --merchant-id=... --api-key-id=... --secret-key=...`. The README's env var names are inconsistent: VISA_ACCEPTANCE_* in one sample, unprefixed MERCHANT_ID/API_KEY_ID/SECRET_KEY elsewhere.
items.tools_exposed: Invoices: create, update, list, get, send, cancel. Payment links: create, update, list, get. Exact function names are not documented. No authorization, capture, reversal or TMS tools.
items.rationale: The scope does not match the hold/capture/reversal design. New in this re-check: the overview says the Invoicing or Pay by Link APIs must be enabled by contacting your account manager. Visa's corporate page says to contact a Visa representative or the Developer Center to request toolkit access. A sandbox may therefore not work out of the box within a hackathon timeline.
items.sandbox_support: configuration.context.environment 'SANDBOX'. A sandbox signup creates a test key, but the APIs may still need enabling.
items.caveats: This MCP gives the agent live write access: it can send invoices and create pay links. Secrets go in as CLI args, which leak into process lists and the stored MCP config. Use sandbox keys only. A community mirror exists at github.com/fastmcp-me/agent-toolkit; do not use it.

items.name: Visa Developer MCP (docs and API reference)
items.install: Remote HTTP. Visa's documented Claude Code JSON: {"mcpServers":{"visa-developer":{"type":"http","url":"https://developer.visa.com/mcp"}}}. The same structure is documented for Codex; verify with `codex mcp list`. CLI equivalent (adapted): `claude mcp add --transport http visa-developer https://developer.visa.com/mcp`. OAuth 2.1 runs in the browser when needed. A Visa Developer account is optional and unlocks more.
items.tools_exposed: Tool names are not listed. Capabilities: read-only public docs and reference data, product/API discovery, OpenAPI-derived schemas, use cases and sample code, semantic search.
items.rationale: Confirmed read-only: 'enforces read-only access and does not handle sensitive customer data'; runtime API invocation is excluded. Useful for TAP and Visa Intelligent Commerce questions. Cybersource REST is better served by the Cybersource MCP and llms.txt.
items.sandbox_support: Not applicable (read-only). The page does not mention a sandbox.
items.caveats: Low risk. Still, never paste credentials into chat.

items.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce product MCP (runtime)
items.install: Not verifiable. The getting-started page (/docs/visa-intelligent-commerce/docs-getting-started#mcp) returned HTTP 403 to fetch. The mcp-docs page only says it executes 'real product actions without managing credentials or auth'. mcp.visa.com redirects (302) to the VIC capabilities page. The visa/ai vic-agent uses it through @visa/mcp-client and needs Visa credentials from .env.example.
items.tools_exposed: Unknown.
items.rationale: Access appears gated (pilot, per Visa corporate). Do not plan around it.
items.sandbox_support: unknown
items.caveats: These are financial-impact tools. Test environments only.

items.name: visa/ai repo: Documentation MCP (sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc), Claude Code skills, VIC packages and reference agent
items.publisher: Official GitHub org visa. MIT (LICENSE confirmed: 'Copyright (c) 2025 Visa').
items.install: Skills, from the README: `git clone https://github.com/visa/ai.git && cp -r ai/skills/<skill-name> <project>/.claude/skills/`. skills/README.md also mentions `npx skills add visa/ai` and user-level ~/.claude/skills. Docs MCP: the official gemini-extension.json configures {"httpUrl":"https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc"} with no auth fields, which suggests no auth but does not confirm it. Claude Code form (adapted, unverified): `claude mcp add --transport http visa-docs https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc`. Gemini CLI: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/visa/ai`. vic-agent: `npm install`, `npm run build:packages --prefix ..`, copy the .env examples, `npm run dev`. Packages @visa/token-manager, @visa/mcp-client and @visa/api-client are workspace packages and were not confirmed on npm.
items.tools_exposed: Docs MCP: get-docs. Skills: visa-best-practices (VDP/VIC, X-Pay token, mutual TLS, MLE/JWE, environments, VIC agent workflows) and visa-acceptance-best-practices. Correction: the second skill is not only card-present. Its README covers card-not-present, digital wallets, Payer Auth/Decision Manager, recurring/stored credentials, Unified Checkout, Click to Pay, webhooks and security keys, plus PAX terminal pathways. It pulls the primary docs live from the Visa Acceptance developer site. vic-agent: LangGraphJS + Next.js demo that supports Claude or OpenAI.
items.rationale: visa-acceptance-best-practices overlaps with the Cybersource skill for the CNP/UC/webhook flow and is a reasonable second reference. visa-best-practices and vic-agent only matter if the team touches Visa Intelligent Commerce. The 'renamed from visa/mcp' claim is unproven: the README just links to both visa/ai/wiki and visa/mcp/wiki, with no rename note.
items.sandbox_support: The docs MCP is on a sandbox host. vic-agent needs Visa credentials, and its README does not mention a sandbox.
items.caveats: Individual SKILL.md files were not read; review them before installing, since they steer the agent. vic-agent touches payment credentials and passkeys and is demo code.

items.name: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) reference implementation
items.publisher: Official GitHub org visa. NOT MIT or another OSS license: LICENSE.md binds use to Visa's Developer Center Terms of Use and the TAP Product Terms.
items.install: Not an MCP; the repo does not mention MCP. Confirmed: `pip install -r requirements.txt`. agent-registry: `python main.py` on :8001. merchant-backend: `python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload` on :8000. cdn-proxy: `npm install && npm start` on :3002. merchant-frontend: `npm install && npm run dev` on :3001. tap-agent: `streamlit run agent_app.py` on :8501.
items.tools_exposed: Streamlit agent that generates signatures, FastAPI backend that verifies them, Node CDN proxy that verifies RFC 9421 signatures, public-key agent registry, and a React sample merchant.
items.rationale: The best reference for signing agent HTTP requests. Overview page re-check: 'Available for use by: Merchants, Independent developers'. It links a rulebook and sample code and mentions no sandbox, signup, SDK or MCP. The earlier claim that the overview says 'in development / not in all markets' could not be reconfirmed.
items.sandbox_support: Local sample only.
items.caveats: License terms are restrictive: read the Visa TAP Product Terms before using the code in a public hackathon repo. Sample keys are for local demo only.

notes:
The adversarial re-check made these changes:
(1) Cybersource Developer MCP is confirmed official on GitHub, PyPI (v0.0.3, 2026-08-04, maintainer developer@cybersource.com) and the docs page. The Claude Code `claude mcp add cybersource-developer-mcp cybersource-developer-mcp start` command is on the docs page only. The README and docs page disagree on .NET support. The README has no skills section. The 'PHP ~3 min' detail was not reconfirmed.
(2) The skill is confirmed verbatim. 'Microform deprecated' applies to the legacy /pts/v2/microform/capture-contexts endpoint, and Microform V2 docs still exist. The skill recommends UC v1.
(3) Visa Acceptance Toolkit/MCP is confirmed (npm 0.0.96, repo-linked). New blocker: Invoicing/Pay by Link must be enabled through an account manager, and access may need a Visa rep. It stays low value.
(4) visa/ai is MIT, but the claim that it was renamed from visa/mcp is unproven. The visa-acceptance-best-practices skill does cover CNP, UC, webhooks and wallets, which corrects 'leans card-present'. Install via `npx skills add visa/ai` is listed in skills/README.md. The official gemini-extension.json points at the sandbox docs MCP with no auth fields.
(5) TAP repo LICENSE is not open source. It binds use to Visa Developer Terms and TAP Product Terms, which matters for a public hackathon repo.
(6) Added the missed official Node SDK (cybersource-rest-client 0.0.84) and the official CyberSource rest-samples-node repo as starter templates.
(7) Visa Developer MCP read-only statement and Codex config are confirmed.
All `claude mcp add` commands except the Cybersource one are adapted from vendor JSON, and none were executed (read-only).
Security: give coding agents sandbox keys only, through gitignored env files. Never pass secrets as CLI args (the Visa Acceptance MCP does this). Never put P12 files or shared secrets in MCP configs. The docs-only MCPs (Cybersource Developer MCP, Visa Developer MCP, Visa docs MCP) need no payment credentials and are the safe choice.
Sources: https://developer.cybersource.com/resources/developer-mcp-sdk.html, https://github.com/CyberSource/cybersource-developer-mcp, https://pypi.org/pypi/cybersource-developer-mcp/json, https://github.com/visaacceptance/agent-toolkit, https://registry.npmjs.org/@visaacceptance/mcp/latest, https://developer.visa.com/resources/mcp-get-started, https://developer.visa.com/mcp-docs, https://github.com/visa/ai, https://github.com/visa/trusted-agent-protocol, https://corporate.visa.com/en/sites/visa-perspectives/innovation/visa-mcp-server-agent-acceptance-toolkit.html, https://www.cs.usc.edu/newsletter/ug-ms-phd-apply-for-la-hacks-2026-at-ucla-april-24-26/, https://lahacks.com/sponsor-us

area: Adversarial verification: supporting infrastructure MCPs (Notion, Browser Use, Anthropic docs, Context7, Supabase, Fly, Railway, Cloudflare, GitHub)

items.name: Notion MCP (hosted remote)
items.install: claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp  then run /mcp in Claude Code and complete the browser OAuth. Default scope is local; --scope project writes .mcp.json and --scope user applies across projects. SSE fallback https://mcp.notion.com/sse is only for clients without Streamable HTTP. stdio bridge: npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.notion.com/mcp. Headless option: an MCP token created by a workspace owner, sent as a bearer token. This needs a Business or Enterprise plan. All of this is confirmed on the fetched page.
items.tools_exposed: About 55 tools on the official list (developers.notion.com/docs/mcp-supported-tools). Search: notion-search, notion-ai-search, notion-memory-search. Read: notion-fetch, notion-list-*-pages, notion-list-page-backlinks, notion-get-file-download-urls. Write: notion-create-pages, notion-update-page, notion-move-pages, notion-duplicate-page, notion-delete-pages, notion-delete-databases, notion-restore-pages, notion-create/update-folder. Data: notion-create-database, notion-update-data-source, notion-create-view, notion-update-view, notion-query-data-sources, notion-query-multiple-data-sources, notion-query-meeting-notes. Files, comments (including create/update/delete and resolve), skills tools, Custom Agent session tools (notion-spawn-session etc.), and users/teams/groups. The researcher's list was accurate but incomplete.
items.rationale: The claim holds. It is the fastest way for the coding agent to design and inspect the planning database. Plan limits matter for this team. On non-Business plans, notion-query-data-sources has a limited query count on one data source at a time, and AI search falls back to keyword search. Use it at dev time only. The deployed agent should use the Notion REST API or SDK, or the CREAO connector.
items.sandbox_support: No sandbox. It acts as the OAuth user on a real workspace, so use a throwaway workspace or teamspace.
items.caveats: The tools include notion-delete-pages and notion-delete-databases, so keep manual approval on. Workspace guests cannot connect. Page content is untrusted input and can carry prompt injection. Integration tokens are not supported on the hosted server.

items.name: Notion plugin for Claude Code (MISSED by researcher)
items.install: Inside Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add makenotion/claude-code-notion-plugin  then  /plugin install notion-workspace-plugin@notion-plugin-marketplace , then restart Claude Code. OAuth goes to the hosted server.
items.tools_exposed: Bundles the hosted Notion MCP (https://mcp.notion.com/mcp), 4 Notion Cookbook skills (Knowledge Capture, Meeting Intelligence, Research Documentation, Spec to Implementation) and slash commands: /Notion:search, /Notion:find, /Notion:create-page, /Notion:database-query, /Notion:create-database-row, /Notion:create-task, /Notion:tasks:setup|build|plan, /Notion:tasks:explain-diff.
items.rationale: This is an alternative to the bare MCP command for the Claude Code users, and the slash commands are a convenience. It adds nothing for the Codex user. Install either this or the bare MCP, not both, to avoid two Notion servers.
items.sandbox_support: Same as the hosted Notion MCP.
items.caveats: The repo shows no releases and has 14 open issues, and its maintenance status is not stated. It has the same write and delete powers as the hosted MCP.

items.name: Notion MCP (local, @notionhq/notion-mcp-server)
items.install: README JSON: {"command":"npx","args":["-y","@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"],"env":{"NOTION_TOKEN":"ntn_****"}}. The Claude Code equivalent below is composed, not from the README: claude mcp add notion-local -e NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_xxx -- npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server. Docker image: mcp/notion. Other env vars: OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS, AUTH_TOKEN and ENABLE_TOKEN_PASSTHROUGH (the last two for HTTP transport).
items.tools_exposed: v2.x has 22 OpenAPI-derived tools. The README names query-data-source, retrieve-a-data-source, update-a-data-source, create-a-data-source, list-data-source-templates, retrieve-a-database, move-page, retrieve-page-markdown and update-page-markdown. post-database-query, update-a-database and create-a-database were removed in 2.0.0.
items.rationale: The README says it is no longer actively maintained and may be sunset. Use it only if the team needs a token-based headless setup without a Business plan.
items.sandbox_support: The integration token sees only pages explicitly shared with it, which is a good least-privilege boundary.
items.caveats: Deprecated: issues and PRs are not monitored. Keep the token out of git.

items.name: Browser Use Cloud MCP (remote)
items.install: claude mcp add -t http -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" browser-use https://api.browser-use.com/v3/mcp  (confirmed verbatim; the legacy x-browser-use-api-key header is still supported).
items.tools_exposed: run_session, get_session, send_task, stop_session, get_session_messages, list_sessions, list_browser_profiles (confirmed).
items.rationale: The claim holds. Browser Use is mainly relevant as a runtime capability inside CREAO. The docs' llms.txt also lists a separate 'Claude Code integration' page, a Browser Use CLI for coding agents, and an agent skill. Note that the docs mark the legacy Cloud 'skills' feature as retired.
items.sandbox_support: Runs in the vendor's cloud browsers. Pricing and free-tier claims were not re-verified.
items.sponsor_expects_use: Unknown, with no LA Hacks link found. Whether this key connects to CREAO's built-in Browser Use is unverified.
items.caveats: Task text and browser profiles go to a third party. Never put Cybersource keys or real card data in tasks or profiles. Vendor pages contain text aimed at AI agents, so treat them as untrusted.

items.name: Browser Use MCP (local stdio)
items.install: claude mcp add browser-use -- uvx --from 'browser-use[cli]' browser-use --mcp  (confirmed). The page lists OPENAI_API_KEY as required and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as the alternative. The Claude Code example has no env block, so add -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... (composed). Optional: BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS, BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_SECURITY.
items.tools_exposed: 16 tools, confirmed: retry_with_browser_use_agent, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_get_state, browser_scroll, browser_go_back, browser_list_tabs, browser_switch_tab, browser_close_tab, browser_extract_content, browser_get_html, browser_screenshot, browser_list_sessions, browser_close_session, browser_close_all.
items.rationale: It overlaps with Playwright and Chrome DevTools MCPs and adds a uv/Python dependency and a second LLM key. Those two MCPs timed out in this session, so this could be a fallback for local browser testing.
items.sandbox_support: Runs locally with access to the browser and file system.
items.caveats: Do not point it at a browser profile that is logged in to payment or bank accounts. BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_SECURITY=true weakens protections.

items.name: Claude Platform Docs MCP
items.install: claude mcp add --transport http claude-docs https://platform.claude.com/docs/mcp  (the URL and Streamable HTTP transport are documented in llms.txt and the server card; the CLI line is composed). No auth: I sent an unauthenticated tools/list probe and got HTTP 200 with a tool list.
items.tools_exposed: Found by a live tools/list probe (the researcher had this as unknown): search_docs(query, limit, sdk_language, kind), get_navigation(tab, format), get_doc(path, sdk_languages), get_api_endpoint(method, ...).
items.rationale: Upgraded from partially to fully verified: the tools are enumerated and no auth is needed. It is useful for current Claude API details. It is still interchangeable with llms.txt or .md fetches and the built-in claude-api skill. llms-full.txt (https://platform.claude.com/llms-full.txt) returned HTTP 200, so that link resolves.
items.sandbox_support: Read-only docs.
items.caveats: Low risk. Treat docs content as untrusted data.

items.name: Context7 MCP
items.install: Official Claude Code commands (from context7.com/docs/resources/all-clients). Remote: claude mcp add --scope user --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp. Local: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp --api-key YOUR_API_KEY. Alternatives: npx ctx7 setup --claude (needs Node 22.13+, does OAuth, generates a key, installs a skill), or the plugin via /plugin marketplace add upstash/context7 and /plugin install context7@context7-marketplace, which needs no API key but does not read CONTEXT7_API_KEY. The key is optional and gives higher rate limits.
items.tools_exposed: resolve-library-id(query, libraryName); query-docs(libraryId, query, language?). CLI: ctx7 library, ctx7 docs.
items.rationale: Confirmed. The researcher's 'composed' remote command matches the official command, and the plugin route was missing. Coverage of the Visa/Cybersource, Photon and CREAO docs is still unchecked, so confirm it with resolve-library-id before relying on it.
items.sandbox_support: Read-only.
items.caveats: Queries go to Context7. Never include secrets or card data. Snippets are third-party content.

items.name: Supabase MCP
items.install: claude mcp add --scope project --transport http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp" , adding ?project_ref=<ref>&read_only=true as recommended. Then run claude /mcp in a regular terminal (not the IDE extension), select supabase and choose Authenticate (browser OAuth). CI: scoped PAT sent as Authorization: Bearer ${SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN}. Query params: project_ref, read_only, features, skip_elicitations. Local stack: http://localhost:54321/mcp.
items.tools_exposed: Confirmed. Database: list_tables, list_extensions, list_migrations, apply_migration, execute_sql. Debugging: query_logs, get_advisors. Development: get_project_url, get_publishable_keys, generate_typescript_types. Edge Functions: list/get/deploy_edge_function, create_edge_function_secret. Account (disabled with project_ref): list/get/create/pause/restore_project, list_organizations, get_organization, get_cost, confirm_cost. Docs: search_docs. Branching (experimental, paid): create/list/delete/merge/reset/rebase_branch. Storage (off by default): list_storage_buckets, get_storage_config, update_storage_config.
items.rationale: The claim holds. It is only worth it if the team picks Postgres/Supabase as the state store. It is already connected in this session.
items.sandbox_support: Use a dev project with read_only and project_ref, or the local CLI stack.
items.caveats: The docs explicitly warn about prompt injection through data rows (iMessage text stored in the database is exactly this risk), say it is for internal dev use only, and say elicitations are not a guarantee. Never store PANs; keep only Cybersource TMS tokens.

items.name: Supabase agent skills
items.install: npx skills add supabase/agent-skills  (project scope by default; --global, --skill NAME, --all for all detected agents).
items.tools_exposed: Skills, not tools: 'supabase' (products, CLI, MCP, migrations, security audits) and 'supabase-postgres-best-practices' (schema, RLS, indexes, queues, performance).
items.rationale: Only relevant if Supabase is chosen. The --all flag can install for both Claude Code and Codex.
items.sandbox_support: N/A
items.caveats: It is a third-party package run through npx, so review it before installing.

items.name: Fly.io MCP (flyctl)
items.install: fly mcp server --claude  (confirmed; documented as '[experimental] Start a flyctl MCP server'). Flags: --server, --port (default 8080), -b/--bind-addr (default 127.0.0.1), --config, -i/--inspector, and the global -t/--access-token. Note that fly.io/docs/... now 301-redirects to docs.fly.io.
items.tools_exposed: The docs do not list tools. The fly-* tool names come only from this session's connected server, including destructive ones such as fly-apps-destroy, fly-orgs-delete, fly-volumes-destroy and fly-secrets-set.
items.rationale: The claim holds. The flyctl CLI is enough, and the MCP is experimental.
items.sandbox_support: None; it acts on the real org.
items.caveats: Destructive tools. Never let an agent set Cybersource secrets unattended. Use a scoped deploy token.

items.name: Railway MCP
items.install: railway setup agent (reuses the railway login session; CLI 5.44.0+) or railway setup agent --oauth. Manual: railway mcp install (or --local), and railway mcp local runs the local server. Hosted: https://mcp.railway.com. No Claude Code-specific command appears in the page source. The composed form claude mcp add --transport http railway https://mcp.railway.com (OAuth) is unverified.
items.tools_exposed: Hosted: whoami, list-projects, create-project, list-services, list/get/set/delete-feature-flag, redeploy, accept-deploy, railway-agent. Local: about 50 tools covering services, environments, deploys, variables, domains, TCP proxies, private networking, templates, buckets and volumes, get_logs and metrics, docs_search and docs_fetch. The local server previews changes and requires confirm:true.
items.rationale: The claim holds. Only useful if Railway is already the chosen host.
items.sandbox_support: None specific. OAuth scopes access to workspaces and projects. Project tokens are rejected.
items.caveats: Review redeploy, accept-deploy, set_variables and railway-agent calls before approving them.

items.name: Cloudflare MCP servers + Cloudflare Skills plugin
items.install: Recommended for Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add cloudflare/skills (bundles the MCP servers, skills and slash commands), or npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/skills. Plain MCP: {"mcpServers":{"cloudflare-api":{"url":"https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp"}}}, with OAuth or a bearer API token. Other servers: docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, containers.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, browser.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, dex/casb, and agents.cloudflare.com/mcp (Agents SDK docs). Legacy /sse URLs are aliases.
items.tools_exposed: Main server: search(), execute() (model-written JS in an isolated Dynamic Worker, covering 2,500+ endpoints at about 1,000 tokens) and docs().
items.rationale: The claim holds. Only relevant for Workers deployment.
items.sandbox_support: None; it acts on a real account. Pick narrow OAuth permissions.
items.caveats: execute() can change anything within the granted scopes.

items.name: GitHub MCP server
items.install: Remote, Claude Code 2.1.1+: claude mcp add-json github '{"type":"http","url":"https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"}}'. Version 2.1.0 or earlier, OR on Windows if add-json returns 'Invalid input' (documented): claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT". Local Docker OAuth: claude mcp add github -e GITHUB_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT=8085 -- docker run -i --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8085:8085 -e GITHUB_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server. Local Docker PAT: claude mcp add github -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=... -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server. Native binary (missed by researcher): claude mcp add-json github '{"command":"github-mcp-server","args":["stdio"],"env":{"GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN":"..."}}', which supports OAuth without a fixed port. Run these in a terminal and restart Claude Code.
items.tools_exposed: Toolsets as listed by the researcher. I did not re-fetch individual tool names.
items.rationale: The claim holds. The gh CLI covers what this team needs. The session's GitHub config currently returns 401.
items.sandbox_support: N/A
items.caveats: Use a minimal fine-grained PAT and keep it out of git. A PAT takes precedence over OAuth. The documented Windows add-json bug is relevant because this machine runs win32.
